Here's a function that hopefully does what you want:

https://gist.github.com/383326861f06716be0366edf8edc01bd

Load it with

source("https://gist.githubusercontent.com/kbroman/383326861f06716be0366edf8edc01bd/raw/bb171a1bfb9a34d2728bf752e1dc4bc028849277/find_large_intervals.R")

Here's an example:

library(qtl)
data(hyper)
find_large_intervals(hyper, 20)

So I constructed 24 linkage groups based on ~6000 markers from ~140 individuals. As a result, the linkage groups were very dense, with many of the chromosomes looking like this:
Since 6000 markers is way more than I need, I think it would be more efficient to cut down the amount of markers further so that there are not a bunch of markers on top of each other. So, for each chromosome I'd only like 1 marker every X centiMorgans, and to drop everything in between.

The find.flanking function helped me obtain the list of markers posted in my last reply. From there, here's the list of markers I'd like to keep:

and I am unsure how to fix it.

Hopefully this clarified a few things.

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] List markers at set centiMorgan spacing?
parts:
Try using the function pickMarkerSubset(). You need to work with one
chromosome at a time. It seeks to find a subset of markers that are some
distance apart.

Regarding your problem with pull.marker, I think you want to take the
2nd column of the flanking object: flanking[,2] rather than flanking[2].

karl
